findings.message: This diff adds two more readers for `git.base_branch`: the awk+sed in base-ref.sh and the GIT_BLOCK/BASE regexes in hooks/branch.ts. The repo already has one, `yaml_val "$config" git.base_branch` in lib/common.sh, which lib/pr-git.sh uses for the base-branch refusal and the PR target. The new copies require exactly two spaces of indent. yaml_val accepts any indent. The new copies also cut the value at `#` with no space before it, while yaml_val only strips ` #` comments. Fix: have base-ref.sh source common.sh and call yaml_val. Make branch.ts match yaml_val's rules exactly, and add a shared table test that feeds the same configs to both.
findings.scenario: config.yaml contains `git:\n    base_branch: develop` (4-space indent, valid YAML). pr-git.sh targets and guards `develop`. base_merge_base and onBaseBranch skip that line and fall back to origin/HEAD or `main`. So `specclaw-verify size` counts against main, done-guard picks its touched set from main, and the branch guard stays silent while the checkout is on develop. Likewise `base_branch: rel#2` is read as `rel#2` by yaml_val but as `rel` by base-ref.sh and branch.ts.

findings.message: The fix for test layouts (lesson: .NET `*.Tests/`, Java/Kotlin, RSpec) adds only the exact spellings that were named. Common variants of the same class are still counted as production: .NET projects named `*.UnitTests/`, `*.IntegrationTests/` or `*.Test/`; Gradle source sets such as `src/integrationTest/`, `src/androidTest/` and `src/testFixtures/`; Go `testdata/`; and Spock/ScalaTest `*Spec.groovy` / `*Spec.scala` outside a test/ folder. Add a pattern for each, such as `**/*.*tests/**`, `**/*.test/**`, `**/*Test/**`, `**/testdata/**` and the cased `**/*Spec.*`, and add those rows to the ROWS table in run-size-cap-tests.sh.
findings.scenario: A branch adds 300 lines in `App.UnitTests/Builders/UserBuilder.cs` and 150 lines of production code, with size_cap 400. The tool reports `450 production lines ... is over the 400-line cap` and exits 1 (FAIL). The correct count is 150.

findings.message: The script runs under `set -euo pipefail` and expands `"${extra[@]}"`. With the template default `size_exclude: ""`, `extra` is an empty array. On bash 3.2 (stock macOS) through 4.3, expanding an empty array under `set -u` aborts with `extra[@]: unbound variable` and exit status 1. Exit 1 is this subcommand's "over the cap" code, so a shell error is read as a FAIL verdict. Guard the expansion with `${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"}` and add a size-cap test that runs under /bin/bash or an empty size_exclude on bash 3.2.
findings.scenario: On macOS with /usr/bin/env bash resolving to bash 3.2, the config has the template's `size_exclude: ""` and the change has 3 production lines. `specclaw-verify size .specclaw 001-x` prints `unbound variable` and exits 1. verify records it as over the size cap (FAIL) instead of `3 production lines (cap 400)`.

findings.message: The review hold embeds the full multi-line output of `specclaw-review verdict`. The caller keeps only lines that start with `hold ` and `skip `. Every line after the first is silently dropped, and an output line that starts with `skip ` would be reported as a guard skip. Collapse `review` to one line (for example, its last line or `tr '\n' ' '`) before echoing it.

cmd_size never checks that `.specclaw/changes/<change_name>` exists. A misspelled change name still counts the branch and reports a pass under the cap. It can only ever miss the waiver. Fail with exit 2 when the change folder is absent. Also, a size_cap with a leading zero (`08`) passes the `^[0-9]+$` check, but `$((cap / 2))` then fails as an invalid octal number. Strip leading zeros with `10#$cap`.

verify.md says the test file names are matched "ignoring case", and the templates/config.yaml comment says "any case". The code matches the CamelCase patterns (`*Test.*`, `*Tests.*`) case-sensitively, on purpose. Change the docs to say that.
